name: Zoom whitening
lead: Zoom whitening is the name commonly given to a branded, light-activated in-office tooth-whitening treatment in which a high-strength hydrogen peroxide gel is applied by dental staff and exposed to a lamp.[1] It belongs to the wider category of in-office power bleaching described on Wikipedia, which uses roughly 25-38% hydrogen peroxide with 6-15 minutes of light exposure.[1]
Evidence specific to the branded system is thin in the sources reviewed; research mostly addresses in-office bleaching generally, including how light intensity and peroxide affect sensitivity.[2][3]

paras: In-office power bleaching begins with a protective barrier on the gums, followed by peroxide gel and a light source such as halogen, LED or plasma arc.[1] Results are often 2 to 7 shades and may last several months, though a share of the change can rebound within a week.[1]

Wikipedia reports that 67-78% of in-office patients experience sensitivity, lasting around 4-39 days, and that improper light use can increase it.[1] A laboratory study of extracted premolars found that bleaching with several in-office protocols altered expression of substance P, a pain-related neuropeptide, in the dental pulp.[2]

Registered trials have compared high-intensity light bleaching with descending-intensity protocols for post-bleaching sensitivity, and tested a newer in-office whitening system for efficacy in 180 adults.[3][4] No results from these registrations are summarised here.

quick.overview:
Zoom whitening is a well-known in-office whitening treatment: a dental professional applies strong peroxide gel and uses a light. It is a form of professional power bleaching.

Wikipedia reports changes of 2 to 7 shades for in-office bleaching, lasting months.
quick.mechanism: Peroxide gel releases oxidising agents that lighten stain inside enamel and dentin; the lamp is intended to speed the process.
quick.risks: Sensitivity is common and usually temporary; gums are protected with a barrier because strong peroxide can burn tissue.
